findings.issue_text: [BUG] Fire-and-forget cancellation calls replace awaited batched deletes in handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings.tsx, and workflows.tsx — unawaited forEach of deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder can drop in-flight Prisma/Twilio work in serverless environments and prevents callers from reporting failure (confidence: 75)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Fire-and-forget cancellation calls replace awaited batched deletes in handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings.tsx, and workflows.tsx — unawaited forEach of deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder can drop in-flight Prisma/Twilio work in serverless environments and prevents callers from reporting failure (confidence: 75)

[BUG] Cron cancel loop in scheduleEmailReminders.ts aborts all remaining reminders on first SendGrid error since the try wraps the whole loop, and the error is only console.log-ed; reminders N+1..end are never attempted and queued delete promises never execute (confidence: 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop in a single `try/catch`. Each iteration does an `await client.request(...)` before pushing the Prisma `delete(...)` promise. If SendGrid `client.request` throws for any reminder, control jumps to the `catch`, so reminders after the failing one are never attempted, and any previously queued `workflowRemindersToDelete` promises are not `await`ed because `await Promise.all(...)` is skipped. This matches the finding: one error aborts processing of the remaining reminders and prevents pending deletes from executing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] immediateDelete path in emailReminderManager.ts cancels the SendGrid batch but returns without marking the row cancelled or deleting it; if the SendGrid call throws, the error is swallowed and the DB row stays scheduled=true so the cron (which only queries cancelled: true) never picks it up and the reminder email still fires (confidence: 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete)` returns early on the `immediateDelete` branch after attempting the SendGrid cancel call, without updating the DB row (`cancelled=true`) or deleting it. Callers in the diff use `immediateDelete=true` (e.g. workflows router when deleting workflows/steps). Separately, `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` only picks up rows with `cancelled: true` to perform cancellation+deletion. Therefore, if the SendGrid cancel attempt fails (caught and only logged), the reminder row remains not-cancelled and will not be retried by the cron logic, leaving the scheduled send intact.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Non-immediate email cancellation only sets cancelled: true without cancelling with SendGrid or deleting the row, relying entirely on the cron running in the hour before scheduledDate; cron outages let the email send anyway and stale rows are never terminally cleaned up (confidence: 50)

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` now defaults to only `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ cancelled: true })` when `referenceId` exists and `immediateDelete` is not set, without calling SendGrid or deleting the row (emailReminderManager.ts). Actual SendGrid cancellation + DB deletion is deferred to the `scheduleEmailReminders` handler, which looks for `cancelled: true` reminders within the next hour and then cancels via `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` and deletes them (scheduleEmailReminders.ts). This does create a reliance on that periodic job running close to `scheduledDate`; an outage/missed run could allow a SendGrid-scheduled email to go out despite the booking being cancelled. However, the claim that rows are “never terminally cleaned up” is not strictly true in the normal path, since the cron explicitly deletes them when it runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] handleNewBooking.ts reschedule wraps a forEach of async unawaited cancellation calls in try/catch, so the catch can never fire and 'log error while canceling' is dead code (confidence: 75)

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the new reschedule block does `try { originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); }); } catch { ... }`. Both deleteScheduled* functions are `async` (return Promises), but the forEach callback does not `await` them (nor is the callback `async` and aggregated). As a result, any rejection/throw inside those async functions will not be caught by the surrounding try/catch, making the error logging effectively unable to capture async failures and potentially causing unhandled promise rejections.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Cron cancel query in scheduleEmailReminders.ts selects all WorkflowReminder rows with cancelled: true with no user/tenant scoping and no method filter; a future SMS row with cancelled set would have its Twilio SID sent to SendGrid as batch_id (confidence: 50)

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cleanup query fetches `workflowReminder` rows with only `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= ...` and then unconditionally calls the SendGrid scheduled_sends cancel API using `reminder.referenceId` as `batch_id` and deletes the reminder (`prisma.workflowReminder.delete`). There is no `method === EMAIL` filter in this code path, so if non-email reminders ever had `cancelled=true` (or if data is inconsistent), this job would attempt to cancel them via SendGrid and still delete the DB row. However, the diff does not show SMS reminders being marked `cancelled` (SMS deletion deletes rows directly), and the lack of user/tenant scoping is plausibly intentional for a global cron-like endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Previously-guarded reminder.scheduled && referenceId check dropped in handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings.tsx, and workflows.tsx; unscheduled email reminders with stale referenceIds get cancelled: true set but are never picked up by the cron, leaving orphaned rows (confidence: 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does drop the `reminder.scheduled && reminder.referenceId` guard, but the new `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` explicitly deletes the DB row when `referenceId` is null, and otherwise marks the row `cancelled: true` (emailReminderManager.ts). The cron/API `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` was updated to query `cancelled: true` reminders and then cancel+delete them, so the claim that they are “never picked up by the cron” isn’t supported by the diff (it now *does* pick up cancelled reminders). The specific scenario of “unscheduled reminders with stale referenceIds” not being cleaned up can’t be verified from the shown code/schema (e.g., whether `scheduledDate` can be null), so the finding overstates what the diff demonstrates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded findMany fetches all cancelled WorkflowReminder rows with no pagination/limit, and cleanup only deletes reminders with scheduledDate within the next hour, so cancelled-but-future reminders accumulate forever — needs index on (cancelled, scheduledDate), a take limit, and stale-row cleanup (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts the new query is not an unbounded fetch of all cancelled reminders; it filters by `cancelled: true` AND `scheduledDate <= dayjs().add(1, "hour")` (so it only targets items scheduled within the next hour). Also, cancelled future reminders are not shown to “accumulate forever” in this diff: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` marks reminders as `cancelled: true` (when not immediate) and the hourly-window cleanup will eventually pick them up as their `scheduledDate` approaches. While adding an index/limit could be a performance improvement, the finding’s core claims don’t match the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sequential N+1: cron handler awaits a SendGrid HTTP request per reminder serially instead of running them concurrently, making runtime linear and unbounded under backlog (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block iterates `remindersToCancel` with `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request(...) }`, which performs one SendGrid HTTP cancellation request at a time (sequential). Only the Prisma deletes are batched via `Promise.all` afterward. This makes the cron runtime scale linearly with the number of reminders to cancel and could become slow under backlog, but it’s a performance/scalability concern rather than a verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Batched deleteMany replaced with per-row N+1 DB writes in deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder, multiplying DB round-trips from 1 to N, with async managers called unawaited in forEach loops (fire-and-forget, no backpressure) (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves Prisma writes into the async reminder-manager functions (e.g., `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` now does `prisma.workflowReminder.update/delete`, and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` does `prisma.workflowReminder.delete`). Call sites invoke these async functions inside `forEach` without `await` (e.g., `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `viewer/bookings.tsx`, `viewer/workflows.tsx`, `handleNewBooking.ts`), so the DB updates/deletes and external cancellations can be left in-flight when the request handler continues/returns, risking reminders not being cancelled/removed reliably. The finding’s “batched from 1 to N” claim is overstated (previous code also looped per reminder), but the unawaited async DB work introduced here is a verifiable correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unawaited async work in workflows.tsx update path: remindersToUpdate.forEach with async callback ignores promises, causing unhandled rejections, TRPC response before cleanup, and uncontrolled concurrent external API calls with no error aggregation (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the update path uses `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... })` (see the block added under `//cancel all workflow reminders from steps that were edited`). The callback is `async` but the returned promises are not collected/awaited, and the internal async calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` are also not awaited. This means the TRPC mutation can complete and respond before reminder cancellation/DB updates finish, and any rejection inside those async operations may become unhandled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: workflowReminders: true include added to rescheduled-booking fetch adds an extra join on the hot booking path (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, the fetch for `originalRescheduledBooking` was changed to `include: { ..., workflowReminders: true }` (added at `+        workflowReminders: true,`). This will cause Prisma to also load the `workflowReminders` relation (typically an extra query or more expensive query plan), which is a real performance/scalability concern on the booking/reschedule request path. It’s not a correctness bug, but it is a concrete diff-grounded cost increase.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deferred cancellation of SendGrid batches relies on the hourly cron; reminders for cancelled/rescheduled bookings can still fire if cron is delayed, unscheduled, or fails

adjudication.rationale: In multiple cancellation/reschedule paths (e.g. handleCancelBooking.ts, viewer/bookings.tsx, workflows.tsx), email reminders now call deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId) without the `immediateDelete` flag. In emailReminderManager.ts this no longer cancels the SendGrid scheduled_send; it only sets `WorkflowReminder.cancelled = true`. Actual SendGrid batch cancellation is deferred to scheduleEmailReminders.ts, which only runs its cancellation logic when that API/cron executes and only for reminders within the next hour. Therefore, if the cron/API is delayed, not running, or fails, the SendGrid batch can still send even though the booking/workflow was cancelled/rescheduled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true cancels the SendGrid batch but leaves the DB row scheduled:true and unmarked, creating orphaned rows never cleaned up (inconsistent with SMS path)

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete)` returns early when `immediateDelete` is true after canceling the SendGrid batch, without updating or deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row (`return;` after the `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` cancel POST). This leaves the DB record intact (e.g., still `scheduled` and not `cancelled`), unlike the SMS path which always deletes the DB row (`smsReminderManager.ts` deletes via `prisma.workflowReminder.delete`). This is exercised in the diff (e.g., `handleNewBooking.ts` cancels reminders on reschedule with `immediateDelete=true`), so it can create orphaned/inconsistent reminder rows that won’t be cleaned by the new `scheduleEmailReminders` cleanup logic (which only targets `cancelled: true`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts rescheduling cancels reminders via unawaited promises in forEach inside try/catch, so async errors become unhandled rejections and the log.error path can never fire

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, the new reschedule block does `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); })` inside a try/catch, but both delete functions are `async` and are called without `await` (and `forEach` doesn’t await). As written, the try/catch cannot catch promise rejections from those async calls, so `log.error(...)` won’t run for async failures. The finding’s “unhandled rejections” part isn’t strictly verifiable from this diff because the delete functions themselves catch/log errors, but the unawaited-async + ineffective try/catch issue is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking change to exported deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder signatures with no compatibility handling for external/forked consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the exported functions’ signatures: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` from `(referenceId: string)` to `(reminderId: number, referenceId: string | null, immediateDelete?: boolean)` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` from `(referenceId: string)` to `(reminderId: number, referenceId: string | null)` in `emailReminderManager.ts`/`smsReminderManager.ts`. Call sites shown in the diff were updated, but there is no overload/compat wrapper preserving the old API, so this is a breaking public API change for any consumers (including other packages not covered by this diff, or external/forked users).

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both note that the new 'cancelled' Boolean field is nullable with no default, so existing records may have NULL instead of false, creating tri-state behavior and potentially incorrect filtering/logic when treating NULL as not-cancelled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cron cancellation block in scheduleEmailReminders.ts swallows all errors including failed DB deletes, uses console.log instead of structured logger, and one bad record can block cancellation of subsequent reminders

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop in a single `try/catch` and does `await client.request(...)` inside the loop. If one reminder cancellation request throws (or later a delete throws), control jumps to the catch and the loop stops, so subsequent reminders won’t be processed ("one bad record can block cancellation of subsequent reminders"). The catch only `console.log(...)`s and does not rethrow, so failures (including failed DB deletes) are swallowed and the cron can silently leave reminders uncancelled/undeleted. The diff explicitly shows `console.log` usage instead of the structured logger used elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: workflows.tsx lines ~901-963 contain whitespace-only reformat blocks mixed into a functional change, polluting the diff/blame

adjudication.rationale: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx around the shown ~901+ hunk, the changes are largely indentation/whitespace-only (e.g., removing leading two spaces on many lines within the example-booking construction block), with no semantic edits. These formatting-only changes are included in the same PR that also makes functional reminder-cancellation changes elsewhere in the file, which does pollute the diff and future blame without providing functional value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder promises not awaited in handleNewBooking.ts try/catch (~line 964-976), causing unhandled promise rejections and log.error never firing

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, the new try/catch wraps a synchronous forEach that calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...) and deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...) without awaiting (lines ~961-976 in the diff). Because these functions are declared async (see emailReminderManager.ts and smsReminderManager.ts), any rejection occurs asynchronously and will not be caught by the surrounding try/catch, potentially leading to unhandled promise rejections and the log.error in the catch not running for those async failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: In smsReminderManager.ts:177-185, if twilio.cancelSMS throws, the prisma.workflowReminder.delete is skipped, leaving the SMS reminder row scheduled=true with no retry path, so the SMS reminder still fires

adjudication.rationale: In smsReminderManager.ts, deleteScheduledSMSReminder wraps both `await twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and `await prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` in the same try block. If `twilio.cancelSMS` throws, control jumps to the catch and the DB delete is skipped, leaving the WorkflowReminder row intact. This is a regression versus the previous pattern in callers (e.g. handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings router) where the Prisma deleteMany ran regardless of whether the Twilio cancel call succeeded (the cancel call was not awaited and DB deletion happened separately). The diff shows no fallback/mark-as-cancelled path for SMS reminders like the new email logic, so a failed Twilio cancel can result in both the external SMS still scheduled and the DB reminder record remaining.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Booking-cancellation handlers in handleCancelBooking.ts:483-494 and viewer/bookings.tsx:484-494 are fire-and-forget without awaiting, so serverless invocations may exit before cancellation writes/API calls complete

adjudication.rationale: In both places cited, the diff replaces previously-awaited Prisma deleteMany promises with calls to async cancellation helpers but does not await those helpers. In handleCancelBooking.ts, the reminder cleanup is now only `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` inside nested `forEach` loops, and `prismaPromises` no longer includes any reminder-related promises, so `await Promise.all(...)` will not wait for reminder DB writes/API cancels. In viewer/bookings.tsx the code similarly loops and calls the async deleteScheduled* functions without awaiting, and the prior `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` was removed. Since the helpers now perform Prisma delete/update and external API calls (per emailReminderManager.ts/smsReminderManager.ts changes), these operations can be left in-flight when the request/procedure completes, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43-76, the try/catch wraps the entire for loop, so one SendGrid failure aborts all remaining cancellations and a bad reminder permanently poisons the queue

P2: In emailReminderManager.ts:210-218, the immediateDelete path cancels the SendGrid batch but leaves the DB row untouched — on error the reminder stays scheduled=true and the cron never retries; on success no DB row cleanup for reschedule path

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete)` has an `immediateDelete` branch that POSTs a SendGrid cancel and then `return`s without updating or deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row. Call sites in the diff pass `immediateDelete: true` (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts` for reschedule cleanup, and `workflows.tsx` when deleting workflows/steps), so those reminders can remain in DB with their prior `scheduled` state and without `cancelled=true`. adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: In workflows.tsx (~572-581), remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) creates unawaited async work for step-edit reminders, so the mutation returns while cancellation writes may still be in flight or silently fail

adjudication.rationale: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx, the new block `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); })` launches async work but the returned Promises are neither collected nor awaited (no `await Promise.all(...)`). Additionally, the async calls inside aren’t awaited. This means the mutation can return before reminder cancellations/DB updates finish, and failures can be missed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Cancelled-but-not-yet-due reminders are never garbage collected in scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-52 — rows that miss the 1-hour cron window (e.g., cron downtime or poisoned queue) accumulate forever

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` the new cleanup queries `workflowReminder` where `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now+1h`. Anything that becomes overdue (even if the cron was down during the intended hour) will still satisfy `scheduledDate <= now+1h` once the job resumes, so the rows are not “never” garbage collected. The diff does not show a condition that would permanently exclude cancelled reminders solely due to missing the 1-hour window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: No cancellation cron equivalent exists for SMS reminders, so any Twilio failure combined with the synchronous deleteScheduledSMSReminder path leaves SMS reminders permanently unrecoverable

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an email-side cancellation/cleanup path (scheduleEmailReminders.ts queries `WorkflowReminder` with `cancelled: true` and cancels/deletes them), and there is no analogous SMS cron shown. However, the specific claim that Twilio failure + the “synchronous deleteScheduledSMSReminder path” makes SMS reminders “permanently unrecoverable” is not supported by the diff: `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` performs the Twilio cancel and the Prisma `workflowReminder.delete` inside the same `try`. If `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` throws, control jumps to `catch` and the DB delete does NOT run, leaving the reminder row present (i.e., not deleted/unrecoverable).

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43-77: findMany selects all cancelled reminders without filtering on method, referenceId, or scheduled; a cancelled reminder with no referenceId is sent to SendGrid with batch_id: null, throwing and aborting the entire loop, preventing SendGrid cancel and DB delete of subsequent reminders

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts the new cancellation block fetches all WorkflowReminder rows with cancelled: true and scheduledDate <= +1h, with no guard on reminder.method or reminder.referenceId. The subsequent loop unconditionally calls the SendGrid endpoint with body.batch_id = reminder.referenceId; if any cancelled reminder has referenceId == null (or is a non-email reminder that shouldn't use SendGrid), client.request can throw. Because the whole loop is inside a single try/catch, the first throw aborts processing of the remaining reminders, so later cancellations/deletes in that batch won't happen.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Call sites (handleNewBooking.ts:964-976, bookings.tsx:486, workflows.tsx:211/375/572): async deletion functions are fire-and-forget and not awaited, so try/catch can never catch errors and they become unhandled promise rejections; route can respond before reminder rows are marked/deleted, allowing reminders to still fire after cancellation

adjudication.rationale: Verified in the diff: multiple call sites invoke async functions without awaiting them. E.g. handleNewBooking.ts wraps `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` in a try/catch but calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` (both `async`) without `await`; `Array.forEach` won’t await, so the try/catch cannot catch async errors and the returned promises may reject unhandled. Similar fire-and-forget calls exist in bookings.tsx and workflows.tsx where the previous `Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` was removed. This also means the request/route can complete before Prisma `update/delete` inside these functions runs (e.g. `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` now does `prisma.workflowReminder.update({data:{cancelled:true}})`), allowing reminders to remain active long enough to still fire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: emailReminderManager.ts:214-220: with immediateDelete=true, only the SendGrid batch is cancelled and the WorkflowReminder row is never deleted or flagged cancelled, leaking rows that remain scheduled:true and are untouched by the cron cleanup

adjudication.rationale: In emailReminderManager.ts, deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete) returns early when immediateDelete is true after cancelling the SendGrid batch, without updating the WorkflowReminder row (e.g., setting cancelled=true) or deleting it. This means callers that use immediateDelete=true (e.g., handleNewBooking.ts reschedule path and workflows.ts delete-step/workflow paths) will leave reminder rows in the DB in their prior state (likely still scheduled=true, cancelled not set). The cron cleanup added in scheduleEmailReminders.ts only targets rows with cancelled: true, so these rows would not be cleaned up by that new logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reminder-cancellation logic (if EMAIL / else if SMS dispatch block) is duplicated across 6 call sites in handleCancelBooking.ts:484, handleNewBooking.ts:966, bookings.tsx:486, workflows.tsx:211/376/573 instead of being abstracted in reminderScheduler/emailReminderManager

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the same reminder-cancellation dispatch pattern repeated in multiple places: handleCancelBooking.ts iterates workflowReminders and does `if (reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.EMAIL) deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId) else if ...SMS...` (around lines ~481+); handleNewBooking.ts adds the same loop for `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders` (around ~961+); bookings router repeats it for `bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders` (~481+); workflows router repeats similar loops for deleting workflows/steps and disabling event types (e.g., around ~208, ~372, ~514, ~569). This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/architecture concern (duplication across several call sites), but it is not a verifiable correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: workflows.tsx:376 vs 211/526: inconsistent immediateDelete semantics — deleting workflow/step uses immediateDelete=true while disabling event types and editing steps use deferred cancellation, so edited/disabled reminders can still send for up to ~1 hour until the cron cancels them

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent usage of the new `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` semantics in `workflows.tsx`: deleting a workflow/step calls it with `immediateDelete=true` (e.g., around the scheduled reminders cancellation for deleted workflow/step), while disabling event types and editing steps call it without the flag (deferred path), which only sets `cancelled: true` in DB (see `emailReminderManager.ts`). Separately, `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` only actually cancels provider scheduled sends for reminders where `cancelled=true` and `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. This creates a real behavioral inconsistency/risk window, but the claim that reminders "can still send for up to ~1 hour" depends on how frequently `scheduleEmailReminders` is executed (not shown in the diff), so it’s not fully verifiable as a definite bug from this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts:52: uses console.log instead of the codebase logger, making SendGrid cancel failures invisible in structured logs

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the newly added cancellation block wraps SendGrid cancellation/deletion logic in a `try/catch` and logs errors via `console.log(`Error cancelling scheduled Emails: ${error}`)`. This is diff-verifiable. Whether this should use the codebase logger isn’t strictly a functional defect, but it is a concrete maintainability/observability concern because it bypasses any structured logging used elsewhere (e.g., `log.error` seen in other files in this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleCancelBooking.ts / bookings.tsx: cancelled email reminder rows (cancelled: true) are never deleted and accumulate indefinitely; the cron delete only handles reminders within 1 hour, so no TTL/cleanup exists for cancelled rows

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds deferred cleanup for cancelled email reminders: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` now marks the DB row `cancelled: true` (unless `immediateDelete` or no `referenceId`), and `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` explicitly queries `workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: now+1h }}})` then cancels the provider send and deletes each reminder row. So cancelled rows are not “never deleted” nor guaranteed to “accumulate indefinitely”; they persist until their scheduledDate is within the 1-hour window, at which point they are deleted by this job.

adjudication_records.issue_text: workflows.tsx:901-960: large whitespace-only reformatting block (indentation stripped) inside a functional PR, obfuscating the diff and risking merge conflicts

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` around the shown block (~923+), the diff includes a large chunk where indentation/whitespace is stripped (e.g., `orderBy: { createdAt: "desc", }`, object literals, and nested fields lose their prior indentation) without any apparent functional change. This kind of formatting-only churn inside an otherwise functional PR makes the diff harder to review and can increase merge-conflict risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:38-44: booking feature directly imports ee/workflows internals instead of using the reminderScheduler abstraction, hard-coupling the booking flow to paid-tier internals and per-method managers

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, the diff adds direct imports of per-channel EE reminder managers: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` from `@calcom/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` from `.../smsReminderManager` (see added imports near the top). It then uses them to cancel reminders on reschedule (`originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)`). This bypasses the existing `scheduleWorkflowReminders`/scheduler abstraction and hard-couples the core bookings flow to EE workflows internals and method-specific managers, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Reminder cancellation is now fire-and-forget with no await — deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called in a plain forEach across handleCancelBooking.ts, viewer/bookings.tsx, and viewer/workflows.tsx, so promises may never settle on serverless handlers and errors are unobservable (regression from previously awaited Promise.all behavior)
matched_golden_ids: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying issue: async reminder cancellation functions (deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder) are invoked inside forEach loops without awaiting, making cancellation fire-and-forget and unreliable (promises may not settle/finish), especially in booking cancel/reschedule and workflow-related code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders — in handleNewBooking.ts the entire forEach is wrapped in a single try/catch and in scheduleEmailReminders.ts the sequential await loop stops on first failure, skipping remaining cancels and the Promise.all delete batch, with errors only logged

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, cancellation is done in a single `try` with a sequential `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request(...) ... workflowRemindersToDelete.push(prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)) }`. If any `client.request` throws, control jumps to `catch`, the loop stops, remaining reminders are not canceled, and the accumulated `workflowRemindersToDelete` are never awaited (so already-collected deletes may also be skipped). This matches the finding’s core claim that one failure can prevent subsequent cancels and the final `Promise.all`, with only logging in `catch`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Migration adds nullable 'cancelled BOOLEAN' with no DEFAULT false and no backfill, so legacy rows are NULL; future 'cancelled: false' queries will silently exclude legacy rows, and the new cron query has no supporting index on cancelled + scheduledDate

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `cancelled` as a nullable column with no default/backfill (`ALTER TABLE "WorkflowReminder" ADD COLUMN "cancelled" BOOLEAN;` and `cancelled Boolean?` in `schema.prisma`). That creates a tri-state (NULL/false/true) which can be problematic if any code later filters with `cancelled: false` (NULL rows would be excluded). While the diff doesn’t show a `cancelled: false` query, the concern is grounded in the schema/migration choice. Also, the new cleanup query in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` filters on `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= ...` without any index being added in the shown migration, which is a legitimate performance review point for a cron-like endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Cron cancellation query has no lower bound and no 'scheduled' filter, so it matches any past-due flagged reminder forever, causing an unbounded retry loop of failed SendGrid cancels and unbounded row accumulation

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cleanup query selects reminders with `{ cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: now+1h } }` but has no lower bound and no `scheduled: true` filter. Because `lte` matches all past dates, any cancelled reminder with a past `scheduledDate` will be picked up on every cron run until it is deleted. The cancellation/deletion is inside a single `try { for (...) { await client.request(...); workflowRemindersToDelete.push(prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)) } await Promise.all(...) } catch { ... }` block; if the SendGrid cancel request fails for any reminder (e.g., invalid/expired batch_id), the catch prevents deletion and leaves the row flagged `cancelled`, causing repeated retries on subsequent cron executions with no backoff/state change. This behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Cancelled email reminder rows are now only cleaned up by the cron's 1-hour scheduledDate window; if the cron misses the window (downtime, failure swallowed by catch), the flagged row is never SendGrid-cancelled nor deleted and can survive indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The cron cleanup in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` is not limited to a narrow “1-hour window” that can be missed: it selects cancelled reminders with `scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().add(1, "hour")... }`, which includes any reminders scheduled in the past as well as within the next hour. So if the cron is down at the exact intended time, once it comes back those rows still match and will be SendGrid-cancelled + deleted. While errors are caught/logged (and could delay cleanup), the specific claim that missing the 1-hour window means the row is never cancelled/deleted isn’t supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: The 'scheduled && referenceId' guard was dropped at all call sites without compensating checks; for SMS rows with an already-fired Twilio job, twilio.cancelSMS throws, the catch swallows it, and the DB row delete is skipped, leaving the reminder row lingering

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, call sites no longer do a separate Prisma delete of workflowReminder rows after attempting SMS cancellation (e.g., handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings router, workflows router now only call deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)). The new deleteScheduledSMSReminder implementation performs `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and then `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` in the same try block; if `twilio.cancelSMS` throws for any reason, the catch runs and the DB delete is skipped, leaving the reminder row undeleted. Previously, Prisma deletion happened outside the cancel call, so a cancel failure wouldn’t block DB cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead try/catch in handleNewBooking.ts:964-977 — deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async, so errors escape the catch as unhandled promise rejections; failed cancellations let reschedule proceed silently with stale reminders and the log.error is effectively unreachable

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the new try/catch wraps a synchronous forEach that calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting or collecting promises. Any failures inside those async operations won’t be caught by this try/catch (it only catches synchronous exceptions), and the handler proceeds to reschedule immediately, so cancellation may not complete before continuing (and in serverless/request-lifecycle contexts may not reliably finish at all). The finding’s “unhandled promise rejections” claim is overstated because the delete* functions shown each have their own internal try/catch, but the core issue (dead/ineffective outer try/catch + not awaiting cancellations) is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same unawaited async forEach pattern in workflows.tsx editStep (~572-580): fire-and-forget cancellations silently drop rejections and the router returns success while old reminders may still fire

adjudication.rationale: In `workflows.tsx` within the editStep flow, the diff shows `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); })` and the previous awaited Prisma deletions were removed. The `forEach` result is not awaited (nor are the async cancellation calls awaited inside), so the router can return before cancellations/DB updates complete, and any rejections can be dropped/unhandled—allowing old reminders to potentially still fire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rescheduled-booking email reminders are SendGrid-cancelled but the WorkflowReminder row is never deleted or marked cancelled with immediateDelete=true; on SendGrid failure (catch = console.log) stale rows remain, reminders still fire for replaced bookings, and rows accumulate unboundedly

adjudication.rationale: In the reschedule flow (`handleNewBooking.ts`), email reminders are cancelled via `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`. But `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`’s `immediateDelete` branch only sends the SendGrid cancel request and then `return`s without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row or marking it `cancelled` (see `emailReminderManager.ts`). Therefore, for rescheduled bookings/workflow deletions using `immediateDelete=true`, reminder rows remain in DB indefinitely. Additionally, on SendGrid cancel failure the function just `console.log`s and does not update DB, so the scheduled send may still fire and the stale row remains. The new cleanup in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` only deletes rows where `cancelled: true`, which `immediateDelete` never sets, so these rows won’t be cleaned up by that path either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleCancelBooking.ts:481-495: for non-immediate email cancellation the manager only sets cancelled=true and defers SendGrid cancellation to a cron block; if the cron isn't run/deployed or its SendGrid calls fail (caught with console.log), cancelled bookings still receive reminder emails

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `handleCancelBooking.ts` now calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without `immediateDelete`, and `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (emailReminderManager.ts) in that case only marks the DB row `cancelled: true` rather than canceling the SendGrid scheduled send. Actual SendGrid cancellation/deletion is deferred to `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which looks like a periodic job and wraps the cancel+delete loop in a broad `try/catch` that only `console.log`s on failure. This creates a real reliability/operational dependency: if the periodic endpoint isn’t invoked or its SendGrid cancellation fails, the SendGrid scheduled email may remain active despite the booking being canceled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43-78 cron cancel block: deletes awaited in one Promise.all inside a broad catch, so a rejection is swallowed, already-pushed deletes are never awaited (unhandled rejections), and reminders whose SendGrid cancel failed are silently skipped forever after the scheduledDate window passes

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts the new cancellation block wraps the whole loop + final Promise.all in a single try/catch. If any `client.request(...)` throws partway through the loop, control jumps to `catch` and `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is never reached, so previously collected `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` operations are not executed/awaited and those reminders remain in the DB (and will be reprocessed on subsequent runs). However, the finding’s claim about “unhandled rejections” and “skipped forever after the window passes” is not supported: Prisma queries typically don’t execute until awaited, and the `scheduledDate <= now+1h` condition will continue to match past reminders, so they wouldn’t be skipped forever.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43-50 cancel block has no pagination/limit, fetching all cancelled reminders due within the hour and issuing sequential awaited SendGrid calls; a mass-cancellation spike can blow the function timeout while the run 'completes' with reminders never cancelled or deleted

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts a new cancellation pass does `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... }}})` with no `take`/pagination, then loops `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` and `await`s a SendGrid `client.request` per reminder (sequential external calls) before batching Prisma deletes. This is a concrete scalability/operational-risk issue introduced by the diff: a large number of cancelled reminders could make the API route run long or exceed typical serverless time limits. The exact timeout/failure behavior isn’t shown in the diff, so it’s better framed as an important non-bug review concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: WorkflowStepContainer.tsx:390 UI regression: condition changed from isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded to only isPhoneNumberNeeded, so sender-id-only steps may lose their input block rendering

adjudication.rationale: In WorkflowStepContainer.tsx the wrapper block rendering condition was changed from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to only `isPhoneNumberNeeded`. From the diff context, the rendered content inside this block is the phone number + verification UI, and there is no remaining outer render path shown for `isSenderIdNeeded` without `isPhoneNumberNeeded`. Therefore, a step that requires only sender-id would no longer render this input container, which is a behavioral/UI regression introduced by this change.
